nodes.title: Get a study to review
nodes.summary: The validator opens a study and the server reserves one of its two human review slots. Opening a study changes the queue, but does not save a judgement.
inputs: An authenticated validator and a choice of normal or hard mode.
Eligible records in unvalidated, two human slots in validation_queue, and the administrator's serving_config priorities.
steps: POST /api/next-pairs resumes an active record in the chosen mode or claims a free slot. It can also reserve a small buffer of upcoming studies.
The claim records the validator, shown_at and, for an active study, started_at. An unvalidated record becomes validation_inprogress.
POST /api/pairs/{queue_id}/start promotes a buffered study when the validator opens it.
saves: PostgreSQL: validation_queue claim fields and unvalidated.validation_status.
refresh: The returned study appears immediately after the API response.
The stale-slot job runs every 2 minutes. Unstarted buffered claims can be released after 45 minutes; started claims can be released after 5 days.
outputs: A reserved study card with a queue_id and record_id.
cautions: A reservation is not a submitted review. The displayed next study may have been prefetched earlier.
Normal and hard mode have separate active-study resumption; switching modes does not submit a parked study.

nodes.title: Draft answers: saved in this browser
nodes.summary: Choosing answers and editing text prepares a draft. The draft is copied to this browser's local storage every 10 seconds; it has not yet reached the shared database.
inputs: Type, original-study and outcome choices, corrections, evidence, and comments entered in the current review card.
steps: The interface updates state.judgement as the validator answers the questions.
_startDraftSave writes the current judgement under flora.draft.{pair_id} every 10 seconds.
When the same active pair is resumed, the interface restores draft text and replays the answer gates.
If the stored review baseline differs from the newly imported type or outcome, the interface asks for those answers to be checked again.
saves: This browser only: localStorage key flora.draft.{pair_id}.
No validation_queue judgement is saved by autosave.
refresh: Edits change the open card immediately; the browser backup runs every 10 seconds.
Draft restoration happens when a reserved record is resumed.
outputs: A recoverable local draft, ready to submit.
cautions: Drafts do not follow the user to another browser or computer.
Clearing site storage removes the local draft. Changes made immediately before closing can precede the next 10-second save.

nodes.title: Submit a judgement
nodes.summary: Submit sends one person's decisions to PostgreSQL. In the normal buffered flow, the interface can show the next study while the save is still pending.
inputs: The current draft, the reserved record_id, and the validator's server-issued session.
steps: submitJudgement creates a payload containing checks, corrections, evidence and notes.
The buffered flow stores the payload in flora.pendingSubmits, clears the separate draft, and shows the next study. A background queue posts the payload to /api/judge.
The server locks the record and its open human slot, checks the values, completes the queue row and copies a review summary to unvalidated.validator_1 or validator_2.
The server updates validator points and runs the consensus decision tree in the same transaction.
Only after the successful response does the browser remove the pending payload and refresh the points and leaderboard.
saves: Before confirmation: browser localStorage flora.pendingSubmits, owned by the validator who wrote it.
After the transaction commits: PostgreSQL validation_queue, unvalidated review summary and workflow state, and validators totals; consensus may also write validated.
refresh: The next card can appear before the database save finishes.
Points, stats and the leaderboard refresh after the server confirms success.
Retryable network/server failures use backoff. Parked failures remain available in the pending-submissions recovery interface.
outputs: One durable human judgement, or an explicitly pending local payload if saving failed.
cautions: Seeing the next card is not proof that the previous review was saved. Check the pending indicator.
The queue belongs to its author and is not sent under another validator's login.
A failed submission is not automatically released just because the network failed; release requires a server-issued failure capability or confirmation that the slot is already closed.

nodes.title: Two reviews, Gemini, and the approval decision
nodes.summary: After two human reviews are complete, the consensus engine compares their answers. It can request administrator review, prepare a result for approval, reject a non-eligible record, or automatically approve a qualifying agreement.
inputs: Completed human_1 and human_2 rows from validation_queue, the original extraction, and validator experience/tier.
Gemini's structured sanity-check or tiebreak response when that branch calls the model.
steps: With fewer than two completed human reviews, the engine returns without a final decision.
A senior rejection is authoritative. Explicit uncertainty or an evidence-quote flag sends the record to need_review.
Matching checks and corrections invoke Gemini as a sanity check. A normal accepted agreement becomes consensus_reached and waits for an administrator.

Automatic approval is allowed only for a plain agreement with matching Gemini, no disqualifying uncertainty/evidence/original-identity issue, and either at least one Trusted/Senior reviewer or two experienced reviewers. Experienced means at least 20 admin-approved records and at most 2 flagged judgements.

If checks match but corrections differ, the result is need_review without a Gemini call. If checks differ, Gemini is a tiebreaker: an eligible one-sided match can yield consensus_reached; otherwise the record needs review.
When both reviewers say neither replication nor reproduction, matching Gemini can reject it. A disputed rejection goes to an administrator.
saves: PostgreSQL unvalidated: validation_status, selected final_* values, llm_validator response, and supporting quality information.
Automatic acceptance also inserts/updates the approved record in validated. Human submissions remain in validation_queue.
refresh: Consensus runs during the request that completes the second review, before that request's database transaction commits.
The admin queue sees the new status on its next fetch.
This step does not itself rebuild the combined flora.csv dataset or publish a GitHub release.
outputs: consensus_reached = prepared for admin approval; need_review = admin decision needed; validated = approved validation record; rejected = excluded from the validation export.
cautions: Two matching reviewers do not always mean immediate approval.
Approval of a validation record and publication of the final combined FLoRA dataset are separate steps.
Gemini output is stored evidence for the decision tree, not an unrestricted database editor.

nodes.title: Skip or report an inaccessible article
nodes.summary: Skip releases a reserved slot without submitting a scientific judgement. Its reason is kept separately so administrators can see recurring problems.
inputs: An open reserved study, a skip reason, and a comment when that reason requires one.
steps: POST /api/skip checks that the current validator still owns an open slot.
It releases the claim and adds a validation_skips audit event in one transaction.
An inaccessible reason marks the record restricted_access so it leaves ordinary circulation.
The record status is restored according to remaining work, the validator's skipped_count increases, and the browser loads another study.
The hard-mode cannot-access action has its own /api/restricted endpoint and routes the record to the review team without a judgement or points.
saves: PostgreSQL validation_skips: validator, record, queue, reason and comment.
PostgreSQL validation_queue: cleared claim; unvalidated: status and any restricted-access flag; validators: skipped_count for Skip.
refresh: The slot is available again after a successful skip transaction unless the record has been restricted.
Skipped/restricted admin views show the change on their next fetch.
outputs: An auditable skip or access report, not a completed human review.
cautions: Skip is different from marking the study scientifically ineligible.

The Skipped escalation summary counts distinct validators, so repeated requests cannot inflate it: more than 5 validators for any reason or at least 2 eligibility/data-quality skips can surface an issue.

nodes.title: Complete an assigned restricted study
nodes.summary: An administrator can assign a restricted study to a particular validator. That person's submitted answer directly prepares the record for approval, without waiting for two ordinary queue reviews.
inputs: An open row in assignments for the signed-in validator and the study's effective current values.
steps: The validator opens the item in My Assignments; the server confirms that the assignment belongs to them.
Submit calls /api/assignment-judge synchronously and the interface waits for the response.
The server writes corrections and a review summary, completes the assignment, clears restricted_access, and awards double points.
A definite eligible answer becomes consensus_reached for admin approval. Explicit uncertainty becomes need_review. A neither-type decision becomes rejected.
saves: PostgreSQL assignments.status and completed_at; unvalidated.final_* fields, validator_1 summary, validation_status and restricted_access; validators totals.
refresh: The assignment list and stats refresh after successful submission; the validator returns to the normal/hard queue.
The result appears in the appropriate administrator queue on the next fetch.
outputs: One completed assigned review and a record ready for the next admin decision.
cautions: A positive assignment answer is not automatically inserted into validated by this endpoint.
This path uses the current effective record, including earlier final_* corrections, as its review baseline.

nodes.title: Senior override: reject
nodes.summary: A Senior validator can immediately mark a reserved record as neither a replication nor a reproduction. This is a special authoritative rejection, separate from the ordinary type answer.
inputs: A Senior validator (tier 2 or higher), an open owned slot, and optional notes.
steps: POST /api/senior-reject checks tier and ownership.
The server completes the senior's queue row with a senior_reject marker, sets the record to rejected, and removes any matching row from validated.
If the partner's human slot is still open, the server fills it with the senior rejection at zero additional points; an already-submitted partner review remains intact.
The consensus engine recognizes the marker and cannot overturn the rejection with a later ordinary review or Gemini result.
saves: PostgreSQL validation_queue rejection evidence; unvalidated status and review summaries; validators points/judgement totals.
The record is removed from the approved validation table, validated.
refresh: The rejection is durable after the request commits; the review card then advances.
Downstream prepared files require their own subsequent preparation/publication cycle.
outputs: A rejected record with attributable override evidence.
cautions: A reproduction is an eligible type; this override is for neither type.
The displayed two matching slots may include the senior's stamped partner slot, not two independent human submissions.

nodes.title: My Judgements and corrections after submission
nodes.summary: My Judgements reads reviews already saved by the server. Opening a history card does not rewrite the submitted review or publish a correction.
inputs: The current validator's completed queue rows, linked extraction/final values, and any reviewer feedback.
steps: GET /api/my-judgements lists the signed-in validator's saved work.
GET /api/my-judgements/{queue_id} returns the detailed review, including corrected and final outcomes/evidence.
Administrator review actions handle decisions that need further scrutiny. Flag for review can return pending approval or an automatically approved record to need_review.
Sending an automatically approved record back removes it from validated; the source-retirement mechanism prevents it continuing to feed the combined dataset.
saves: Opening My Judgements: no new scientific data is written.
An admin Flag for review writes unvalidated status/notes and admin_decisions; for an auto-approved record it also removes the validated row.
refresh: Saved history appears after the server confirms submission and the history list is fetched again.
Admin decisions become visible on the next detail/list fetch.
outputs: An audit view of what the person submitted, current final values, and any feedback.
cautions: There is no ordinary validator redo/edit-submitted endpoint in the current API. Change an unsent draft before Submit; a saved review needs the review-team workflow.
Flag for review is an administrator action on the record, not a reset that erases the original human submissions.

nodes.title: Observatory disagreements: separate review lane
nodes.summary: The optional Disagreements feature collects two Trusted/Senior judgements on imported Observatory disagreements, then asks an administrator to approve an answer and separately add it to Source Records.
inputs: Imported records in the separate adjudication schema and a validator with tier 1 or higher.
The feature must be enabled and successfully initialized.
steps: A validator claims one disagreement, chooses the original study/outcome, and submits. Claims have a 60-minute availability window.
Each submitted answer is stored in adjudication.judgements and adds to the validator's regular points total.
After two submitted answers, adjudication.records becomes awaiting_approval. This lane does not call the ordinary consensus/Gemini engine.
Admin Approve stores the selected answer in adjudication.final and marks it approved. An admin who judged that record cannot approve it.
Admin Publish then inserts or refreshes a source_records row and marks the adjudication record published. Subsequent FLoRA preparation is still needed for prepared data/output.
Withdraw soft-deletes that source row and returns the disagreement to approved; reviewed source rows are protected from overwrite or withdrawal here.
saves: PostgreSQL adjudication.records, adjudication.judgements and adjudication.final.
Publish adds a source_records row; Withdraw marks that row deleted rather than physically removing it.
Regular validators totals include disagreement points.
refresh: Submit waits for server confirmation before moving on.
After two answers, the admin list can show awaiting approval on its next refresh.
Approval and Publish are two separate clicks and two separate persistence steps.
outputs: Reviewed disagreement evidence, an approved final answer, and optionally a new Source Records input to the combined pipeline.
cautions: Published in this lane means copied to Source Records; it does not mean a GitHub dataset release has been created.
Skip records that this validator passed on the item and prevents it being served to that validator again.
The feature is optional, so the tab may be absent or unavailable when ADJUDICATION_ENABLED is off.

nodes.title: Where the review data lives
nodes.summary: PostgreSQL is the shared durable store. Raw candidates, individual judgements, approved validation records and prepared FLoRA records are separate tables with different jobs.
inputs: Extractor imports, human and admin actions, source-sheet synchronization, and preparation runs.
steps: unvalidated holds each imported candidate, workflow status, raw extraction, review summaries and final_* corrections. Its name does not mean every row is still awaiting review.
validation_queue holds the two human review slots plus the LLM slot; record_metadata holds additional extraction/provenance fields linked to the candidate.
validated holds approved validation records. It is an input to later combined-dataset preparation, not the entire combined FLoRA database.
source_records combines sheet rows and approved inputs. flora_records is the identity/provenance registry used for combined records.
flora_data holds the complete prepared FLoRA rows for public lookups. It has its own persistent IDs, order and retirement state.
Separate history tables preserve skips, admin decisions, merges, source edits, FLoRA changes, checks and run records.
saves: Shared server PostgreSQL selected by DATABASE_URL; the guide does not expose or require its credentials.
Local browser drafts/pending submissions are distinct from these server tables.
CSV/report files are exported artifacts, not a replacement for the underlying review tables.
refresh: Review tables change when their API transactions commit.
Prepared flora_data and generated files change when their own preparation/store steps complete, rather than at every field edit.
outputs: A traceable chain: unvalidated → validation_queue decisions → validated → source_records → prepared flora_data, with source-sheet rows joining at source_records.
cautions: Do not confuse validated (approved extractor reviews), flora_records (registry), and flora_data (prepared public rows). They answer different questions.
Database state can be newer than a CSV download or published release.

nodes.title: Which ID belongs to which record?
nodes.summary: The application uses different IDs for the imported paper pair, each human review slot, source-sheet rows and the final public dataset. These IDs are related but are not interchangeable.
inputs: An extractor pair identifier, internal database rows, and permanent combined-dataset identities.
steps: unvalidated.record_id is the internal candidate UUID. Its pair_id identifies the extractor's pair.
validation_queue.queue_id identifies a review slot; its record_id links back to unvalidated and its validator_id links to validators.
validated.record_id also refers to the original unvalidated candidate.
source_records has its own record_id and display_id. flora_records links the primary and merged sources, pins a flora_id, and reserves publication export_id/export_position.
flora_data.id is the permanent prepared/public identity; id_md5 is generated from that ID. Retired positions and identities are not recycled.
saves: PostgreSQL keys, foreign-key links, registry provenance and generated ID hashes.
refresh: Corrections to DOI/title do not imply a new public record ID.
Registry/source associations can change during preparation while publication identity stays pinned.
outputs: A stable way to follow a candidate, review evidence, source lineage and public record without treating a DOI correction as a new identity.
cautions: The extractor pair_id and public flora_data.id_md5 are different concepts even if both look like hashes.
Prepared flora_data deliberately has no cascading foreign key to a source row: a published record can outlive its source.

nodes.title: What a successful server save means
nodes.summary: A normal API operation groups its database changes into one transaction. They commit together on success, or roll back together if the operation raises an error.
inputs: A browser API request and a pooled PostgreSQL connection.
steps: The route enters with db(), which borrows a connection through db_pool.cursor.
Related SQL writes run within that transaction. For a judgement this includes the completed slot, review summary, points and consensus effects.
Leaving the context successfully commits; an exception rolls back. The connection is then returned to the pool if reusable.
The browser reflects the response or retains pending work if it has not obtained confirmation.
saves: PostgreSQL after commit, independently of the browser tab remaining open.
refresh: Other requests can observe the committed data on their next read.
The current screen may need its own fetch/poll; a committed database write does not push every open admin tab to a new view.
outputs: A committed operation or a rolled-back operation; a separate pending-browser state can exist when response delivery is uncertain.
cautions: Local browser autosave and exported filesystem artifacts do not participate in this database transaction.
This describes the ordinary API database wrapper; maintenance tools can have their own transaction and stage boundaries.
